subject: Guidance on Conducting MGCFA with Ordered Data Using lavaan and semTools

messages.author: b742296e4d6ce88e
messages.subject: Guidance on Conducting MGCFA with Ordered Data Using lavaan and semTools
parts:
Hello,

I am currently conducting a Multigroup Confirmatory Factor Analysis (MGCFA) with ordered data and have come across various materials online. However, I am seeking comprehensive guidelines on performing these analyses using lavaan and semTools.

My model is relatively simple:

MgCfa01 <- '
  Fact01 =~ AmasS01 + AmasS02 + AmasS03 + AmasS04 + AmasS05 + AmasS06 + AmasS08 + AmasS09
'

ModMGCFA01 <- sem(model = MgCfa01, data = x, std.lv = TRUE, group = "sex", ordered = c("AmasS01", "AmasS02", "AmasS03", "AmasS04", "AmasS05", "AmasS06", "AmasS07", "AmasS08", "AmasS09"))

ModMGCFA02 <- sem(model = MgCfa01, data = x, std.lv = TRUE, group = "sex", group.equal = c("loadings"), ordered = c("AmasS01", "AmasS02", "AmasS03", "AmasS04", "AmasS05", "AmasS06", "AmasS07", "AmasS08", "AmasS09"))

ModMGCFA03 <- sem(model = MgCfa01, data = x, std.lv = TRUE, group = "sex", group.equal = c("loadings", "thresholds"), ordered = c("AmasS01", "AmasS02", "AmasS03", "AmasS04", "AmasS05", "AmasS06", "AmasS07", "AmasS08", "AmasS09"))

I have a few questions that I hope you can assist me with:

  1. Does lavaan automatically select the appropriate estimator for ordered data? If not, which estimator would you recommend using?
  2. Can I only test for configural invariance, weak invariance (loadings), and strong invariance (loadings and thresholds) with ordered data?
  3. Which fit indices should be reported (scalar, robust)?
  4. Is there a built-in method for comparing two or more models, for example, using semTools?
  5. Which fit indices would you recommend reporting (e.g., CFI, TLI, RMSEA, and SRMR)?
  6. When comparing the Comparative Fit Index (CFI), for two models should I compare the robust or the scalar CFI?
  7. Are there any tutorials or guidelines online that you would recommend? I would be happy to cite any relevant tutorial if available.
  8. I had some missing pattern in one item and I decided to remove it, but I was wondering if there is any way to also include this item (error: lavaan->lav_samplestats_step1():      some categories of variable `AmasS07' are empty in group 1)

Thank you very much for any help you can provide.

David

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Guidance on Conducting MGCFA with Ordered Data Using lavaan and semTools
parts: 1. Does lavaan automatically select the appropriate estimator for ordered data? If not, which estimator would you recommend using?

When you declare any endogenous variables as ordered=, the default is DWLS estimation.  The SEs and model-fit test will be corrected to account for the two-stage estimation (first thresholds+polychorics, then fit the SEM to those).
1. Can I only test for configural invariance, weak invariance (loadings), and strong invariance (loadings and thresholds) with ordered data?

Search the forum for posts about measurement invariance with categorical indicators.  Your order is wrong, perpetuated by decades of bad advice.  Read the Wu & Estabrook (2016) reference on the ?semTools::measEq.syntax help page, and follow the examples.
1. Which fit indices should be reported (scalar, robust)?
The ones labeled "robust" are consistent estimates of the index that would be obtained from normal data.
1. Is there a built-in method for comparing two or more models, for example, using semTools?
1. Which fit indices would you recommend reporting (e.g., CFI, TLI, RMSEA, and SRMR)?
No single-number summary is really useful to describe why a model fails to reproduce the data.
1. When comparing the Comparative Fit Index (CFI), for two models should I compare the robust or the scalar CFI?
That is not a valid way to test equivalence of 2 nested models.
1. Are there any tutorials or guidelines online that you would recommend? I would be happy to cite any relevant tutorial if available.

1. I had some missing pattern in one item and I decided to remove it, but I was wondering if there is any way to also include this item (error: lavaan->lav_samplestats_step1():      some categories of variable `AmasS07' are empty in group 1)

You can collapse 2 adjacent categories to avoid that.  It is possible to fit models with different parameters per group, but that takes a lot more effort to manually specify all your syntax.
